trends.singleHint: Drag across a period or down a group to see a trend.
trends.single: Its outermost electron has n = {{n}} and feels Z<sub>eff</sub> = {{zEff}}: the nuclear charge Z = {{z}} minus shielding S = {{s}}.
trends.period: Across period {{period}}, n stays {{n}} while Z<sub>eff</sub> rises from {{zEffFirst}} to {{zEffLast}}. Each added electron joins the same shell and shields only part of the added proton, so the outer electrons are pulled harder at about the same distance.
trends.group: Down group {{group}}, n grows from {{nFirst}} to {{nLast}} while Z<sub>eff</sub> changes from {{zEffFirst}} to {{zEffLast}}. Each new shell is farther from the nucleus and is screened by all the shells inside it, so distance wins.

period.ionizationEnergy: So removing an electron gets harder: ionization energy rises, {{first}} → {{last}}.
period.electronAffinity: So atoms generally release more energy when they gain an electron: {{first}} → {{last}}.
period.electronegativity: So atoms pull shared electrons harder: electronegativity rises, {{first}} → {{last}}.
period.zEff: Z<sub>eff</sub> rises by about 0.65 per element in the s and p blocks (+1 proton, +0.35 shielding), but by only 0.15 across the 3d series (+1 proton, +0.85 shielding).

group.ionizationEnergy: So the outer electron is easier to remove: ionization energy falls, {{first}} → {{last}}.
group.electronAffinity: So an added electron is held less tightly, and electron affinity generally falls: {{first}} → {{last}}.
group.electronegativity: So atoms pull shared electrons less: electronegativity falls, {{first}} → {{last}}.
group.zEff: Z<sub>eff</sub> changes little down a group; what changes is n, the shell the outer electron is in.

anomalies.pBelowS: {{from}} → {{to}}: the new electron goes into a p orbital, which is higher in energy and partly shielded by the filled s pair, so it is easier to remove.
anomalies.pairing: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{to}} has the first paired p electron. Repulsion inside the shared orbital makes it easier to remove.
anomalies.nobleGasRadius: {{from}} → {{to}}: noble gases form almost no bonds, so their covalent radii are estimates and not strictly comparable.
anomalies.dContraction: {{from}} → {{to}}: ten 3d electrons sit between them and shield poorly, so {{to}}'s outer electrons feel a higher Z<sub>eff</sub> than expected (the d-block contraction).
anomalies.dBlockFlat: {{from}}–{{to}}: the added electrons go into the inner d subshell and shield the outer s electrons well (0.85 each), so Z<sub>eff</sub> and the properties change only a little, and irregularly.
anomalies.unboundAnion: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{to}}'s s subshell is full. An added electron would go into a higher p orbital, so the anion is not stable.
anomalies.halfFilledP: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{to}}'s p subshell is half filled. An added electron must pair up, so less energy is released.
anomalies.fluorineCrowded: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{from}} is so small that an added electron is crowded by the others in the n = 2 shell, so {{to}} releases more energy.
anomalies.newShell: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{to}}'s outer shell is full. An added electron would start a new shell, screened by everything inside it, so the anion is not stable.
anomalies.filledS: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{to}}'s s subshell is full. An added electron must go into a higher subshell, so the anion is barely stable and little energy is released.
anomalies.relativistic: {{from}} → {{to}}: in period 6 the inner electrons move so fast that relativity pulls the 6s and the first two 6p electrons closer in. {{from}}'s two 6p electrons fill that lower pair, so {{to}}'s third 6p electron sits higher and is easier to remove.
anomalies.estimatedRadius: {{from}} → {{to}}: {{to}} is so radioactive that very few of its compounds have been measured, so its covalent radius is only an estimate.
anomalies.irregularEN: {{from}} → {{to}}: Pauling electronegativities of the heavy p-block are uncertain and depend on the oxidation state used (lead's 2.33 is for lead(IV)), so this small reversal is not meaningful.
anomalies.lanthanideContraction: {{from}} → {{to}}: fourteen 4f electrons sit between them and shield poorly, so {{to}}'s outer electrons feel a higher Z<sub>eff</sub> than expected, and the usual change down the group stalls or reverses (the lanthanide contraction).
anomalies.lanthanideSeries: {{from}}–{{to}}: the added electrons go into the deep 4f subshell, which barely affects the outer 6s electrons, so the properties change little; the radius shrinks slowly across the series (the lanthanide contraction).

shielding.shieldedPercent: {{percent}}% of the nuclear charge is shielded.
